chapter_theme: Meditation (தியானம்), the seventh limb: the gaze turned inward to the light at the palate, between the brows or at the tip of the nose, the ten inner sounds heard only by the devoted, and Siva found at the end of nada. Done rightly it steadies mind and breath, keeps the body and, by grace, takes the devotee past the tattvas and maya.
structure_note: After a definition (598), the chapter treats meditation on inner light (599 to 605), on inner sound (606 to 610), on the chambers and mandalas of the yogic body (611 to 616), and ends with grace beyond the tattvas (617).

598.reading: Meditation, which comes among the limbs counted from the first, is the unwavering intellect's dealing with the senses' enjoyment; meditation on Shakti in form, on the Supreme, and on Siva who comes as guru are the parts of yoga.
598.nuance: ஈரெட்டு (two eights, sixteen) is unclear: it may count the limbs or a larger list of disciplines. புலன்போக மேவல் can be split to mean either settling in the senses' objects or the intellect not going after them; the second fits the chapter better.

599.reading: Within the gathering of eye, tongue, nose, ear and knowing there is one ancient Being who tunes them; showing an unbroken light within the palate, he wore us down and so saved us.
599.nuance: The verse rhymes கண்ணாக்கு, பண்ணாக்கி, அண்ணாக்கு, புண்ணாக்கி. புண்ணாக்கி may mean 'wounding' us or, with the variant பிண்ணாக்கி, crushing us like oil-cake; either way the saving comes through being broken. The palate (அண்ணாக்கு) as a seat of inner light is a yogic teaching.

600.reading: If one looks to the full at the light in the eye that cannot be reached and stays merged there, the way of the sky opens, runs on until the open space is seen, and what stands unmade can be seen.
600.nuance: ஒண்ணா நயனம் (the eye one cannot attain) is commonly taken as the inner or third eye. விண்ணாறு (sky-river or sky-path) and வெளி (open space) are yogic terms whose exact sense I can't fix.

601.reading: Not once do people contemplate the life within the body, not once Siva within the life, not once the mind where Siva dwells, not once the moon-flower.
601.nuance: The four lines step inward, from body to life to Siva to the mind that holds him. சந்திரப் பூ (moon-flower) is traditionally the moon region at the crown of the head; it cannot be fixed from the verse.

602.reading: Light the lamp of the mind to its full, press the lamp of anger until it goes out, and trim every lamp's wick alike: then the lamp of the mind becomes a lamp that does not die.
602.nuance: மாயா விளக்கு means 'an undying lamp', and may also play on மாயை. Anger is itself called a lamp, one burning the wrong way, so meditation needs a moral step as well as a technique.

603.reading: Though one sit in yoga eight thousand years, no one sees and knows the nectar in the eye; if one looks within the inner channel until light comes, he stands merged in it as in a mirror.
603.nuance: உண்ணாடி can be உள் நாடி (the inner nadi) or 'seeking within'. The verse sets long practice against the right inward look: duration alone yields nothing. Sengalvaraya cites Kandar Alangaram 85 as a parallel.

604.reading: If both gazes are set at the middle of the nose, there is no withering, no ruin for the house, no running, no feeling, no self, no seeking: we become Siva.
604.nuance: மனை (house) is usually taken as the body. The run of 'no' clauses describes the stilling of breath, sense and ego; சிவனவ நாமே (we are he, Siva) states identity outright. The variant வேட்டமும் (desire) for தேட்டமும் (seeking) is close in sense.

605.reading: Setting both eyes on the nose and holding within the breath that does not rise, for those who can rest in absorption, seeking the end of sorrow, this is the fruit: the body is without fear.
605.nuance: தூங்க (to sleep) is taken in the yogic sense of absorbed stillness, as often in Tirumular. நாடியே can be 'seeking' or 'by the nadi'. உயர்வெழா வாயு is unclear: breath that is not let rise, or held so it rises within.

606.reading: Bell, sea, elephant, long flute, cloud, the bee, the humming beetle, conch, drum and lute: these ten softened inner sounds cannot be perceived except by those who have bowed.
606.nuance: The list is the yogic ten sounds (dasa nada) heard in meditation. The condition the verse sets is humility or devotion (பணிந்தவர்), not technique.

607.reading: The sound of sea and clouds and elephant, the vina rising in the world of the gods, the flute with abiding light, and the curling conch: none but the yogi who knows steadiness can know them.
607.nuance: A second list of inner sounds, this time conditioned on the yogi's firmness (திடம்), where 606 asked for humility. சுடர்மன்னு வேணு (flute with abiding light) has variants சுடர்மனு and சுடர்மணி and is unclear.

608.reading: The Lord's nature, the host of the gods and the working of the bonds all stand in sound; for those able to perceive it, the Lord is a sound that spreads like its own fragrance.
608.nuance: Lines 2 and 3 are compressed and the syntax is uncertain. The comparison of sound to fragrance suggests a presence that pervades without being seen; the reading that all three stand in nada is the usual one, not the only one.

609.reading: At the end of nada the good lady dwells, at the end of nada is good yoga, at the end of nada is the aim, at the end of nada is the one whose throat held the poison.
609.nuance: நாத முடிவு (nadanta, the end or limit of sound) is where sound subsides into its source. நல்லாள் is traditionally Shakti and நஞ்சுண்ட கண்டன் is Siva, so the verse places both beyond sound. நாட்டம் can be 'the gaze' or 'the goal'.

610.reading: When, among the six that rise and the five inner fires, the deep darkness lifts and nada subsides among the five that oppress, one can reach the anklets of the Lord of the konrai, the goal.
610.nuance: ஆறு (six) is commonly taken as the six centres, அங்கி ஐந்து as five fires and ஐவர் as the senses, but none is fixed by the verse. The variant ஐவர் அருள்நாதமோடும் gives a different syntax for line 3.

611.reading: In the bedchamber it is day and there is no darkness; in the chamber of fire one can keep it from blazing; in the bright pillar the way is a yojana long; in the silver chamber there is no dawn.
611.nuance: The four chambers are taken as places in the yogic body, perhaps the heart, the fire at the base, the spinal channel and the moon region at the crown. ஒள்ளி தறியிலோ ரோசனை is obscure and the whole verse rests on symbols I can't fix.

612.reading: For the yogi who keeps his vow undiminished, becomes one, runs up the spine and reaches the head, once he has grown alike in all three mandalas, the body too stays an aeon without parting.
612.nuance: தண்டு (staff) is usually the spinal channel and the three mandalas are traditionally fire, sun and moon. பிண்டமும் (the body too) implies the life stays with it. ஊழி may be literal (an aeon) or a way of saying 'very long'.

613.reading: There is a way in which each one's mandala comes; in each one's mandala are that one's gods; when each one's mandala comes to that one, each one's mandala is illusion to others.
613.nuance: மாயமற் றோர்க்கே can be split as மாயம் மற்றோர்க்கு (illusion to others) or மாயம் அற்றோர்க்கு (for those free of illusion). On the first, inner attainment is private; on the second, it belongs only to the undeluded. Who அவ்வவர் (each of them) are, practitioners or deities, is also open.

614.reading: If, inside the dark chamber of the weakening heart, one unites with the three mandalas that spring up there and pierces the great bond of the passage, the ascent comes without weariness.
614.nuance: துளைப் பெரும் பாசம் (the great bond with an opening, or of the passage) and மார்க்கழி ஏற்றம் are obscure; மார்க்கழி may be the month or a form of மார்க்கம் (the way). The heart is called dark and weakening before the practice.

615.reading: To end the covering of the three gunas, close the breath firmly at the base, turn it and hold it, and master the right and left by the measure of time: then the King of the gods grants the high state.
615.nuance: வலமிடம் (right and left) is taken as the two nostrils or the two channels, and நாழிகை as a timed measure of breath. வானவர் கோன் here is presumably Siva, not Indra.

616.reading: Those who can stay four fingers above the navel and two fingers within the seat of speech, deep as the sea, and contemplate there have known the Lord of the body.
616.nuance: நடலித்த, மடலித்த and கடலித்து are rare forms and may be corrupt; வாணி (speech, or its goddess) is usually taken as the throat. The finger measures locate centres in the yogic body. சடலத் தலைவன் (lord of the body) is Siva as indweller.

617.reading: Going beyond the thirty-six that are called real to knowledge, and shattering dense maya by grace, the devotees on the path have known the state in which great grace stays unparted.
617.nuance: ஆறாறு (six sixes) is the 36 tattvas. The variant அறியா யசந்தென்னு would call them 'unknowing, unreal' (asat), which fits Siddhanta teaching better than 'real to knowledge'. The verse gives the last step to grace and to the devotee (அன்பர்), not to technique.

links.note: Both call the yogic body a bedchamber (பள்ளி அறை): in 594 it is the great chamber with two doors where held breath lets one live long, in 611 the chamber where it is always day.
Both promise the yogi the body's survival for an aeon (ஊழி): 591 through binding the breath at the lower door, 612 through rising up the spine through the three mandalas.
Both measure the yogic body from the navel in fingers: 580 places coiled kundalini four fingers below it, 616 places the point of contemplation four fingers above.

source_issues: 599: variant பிண்ணாக்கி for புண்ணாக்கி changes the image (oil-cake against wounding).
610: variant ஐவர் அருள்நாதமோடும் for ஐவருள் நாதம் ஒடுங்க changes the syntax of line 3.
611 line 3 (ஒள்ளி தறியிலோ ரோசனை நீளிது) and 616 (நடலித்த, மடலித்த, கடலித்து) are obscure and may be corrupt.
617: variant அறியா யசந்தென்னு ('unknowing, unreal') for அறிவாய சத்தென்னு ('real to knowledge') reverses the description of the 36 tattvas.
